prompt.brief: Design a cluster-health monitoring system that discovers nodes, collects heartbeats and resource signals, detects quorum or capacity risks, and serves reliable operator views.
successSignals: Define node identity, heartbeats, leases, metric labels, health states, clock/skew handling, cluster membership, and quorum semantics.
Separate liveness from performance and application health; handle partitions, flapping nodes, stale heartbeats, autoscaling, and cardinality limits.
Keep node agents lightweight and stream telemetry into bounded aggregates, with durable snapshots for incident investigation.
Explain alert hysteresis, regional failure, secure enrollment, retention, operator access, observability, and degraded status reads.

functional: Enroll and discover nodes, receive heartbeats and CPU/memory/disk/network metrics, and compute node and cluster health.
Expose current status, historical trends, capacity summaries, quorum warnings, topology, and evidence behind each alert.
Support node replacement, maintenance suppression, secure agent rotation, alert acknowledgment, replay, and recovery after collector loss.
nonFunctional: Reflect heartbeat loss within 30 seconds and serve p95 health queries under 300ms.
Scale to 10k nodes per cluster and frequent autoscaling without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 10k nodes per cluster sending heartbeats every 10 seconds
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Cluster-health monitoring system commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Cluster-health monitoring system writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Cluster-health monitoring system version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Cluster-health monitoring system by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Cluster-health monitoring system work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Cluster-health monitoring system projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Cluster-health monitoring system projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Cluster-health monitoring system records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Cluster-health monitoring system latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
